fix(docs): docs:dev serves pages again — a docs bundle hands NODE_ENV back (rich-example-card-b5rz.b5s)

Vite's in-process `build` sets NODE_ENV to "production" when it is unset.
`[demo].paths.ts` bundles the live library (via `demoCard`) while VitePress
resolves its config, before the dev server resolves its own, so `docs:dev`
came up with DEV false and every page threw `__VP_HASH_MAP__ is not
defined`. `bundle` now restores the host's value, or its absence, when the
last overlapping bundle ends.

feat(docs): edits reach a running program that accepts them without restarting it (rich-example-card-b5rz.auo) (#361)

* feat(docs): an edit reaches a running program that accepts it without a restart (rich-example-card-b5rz.auo)

A program opts in through a subset of Vite's import.meta.hot (accept,
dispose, data). The worker runs an accepted edit in the process it is
already running in: dispose callbacks, then every timer and process
listener the last version left is cleared, then the new files run with
the same per-file data. A program that never accepts is declined and the
page restarts it as before. No CardOptions field: the program's accept()
is the one switch.

import.meta is rewritten per file using Sucrase's internal tokenizer,
pinned by a test. The effects kit carries its clock through dispose.

* fix(docs): import.meta reads only hot, a program version has a file, one Sucrase parser on the page (rich-example-card-b5rz.auo)

- Any read of import.meta but .hot is refused at its line, as a syntax
  error is, rather than undefined in the browser and a value in Node.
- Docs fences type-check against import.meta.hot, which every docs
  terminal binds.
- Version = readonly [RunFile, ...RunFile[]] at every seam; a bundled
  script has files: null, and an edit of it restarts it.
- The page aliases Sucrase's parser to its ES build: the playground chunk
  carries one parser, 365 KB -> 209 KB.
- The bundled-path refusal names the construct it refuses.
- Hot-replacement tests stop their 1 ms timers.

* docs(theme): liveOutlet's opened code parsed on either path, the build's or an edit's (rich-example-card-b5rz.auo)
